newsitem.title: CANADA: No risk of frost seen on Canada's Prairies Friday.
newsitem.headline: No risk of frost seen on Canada's Prairies Friday.

text.p: No risk of frost was expected anywhere in Canada's Prairie grainbelt Friday morning, an Environment Canada meteorologist said.
"There's no risk of frost on the Prairie grainbelt Friday morning. There's extensive cloud cover and it's warm enough in (Alberta's) Peace River," meteorologist Jay Anderson said.
A low pressure system over central Saskatchewan Thursday was forecast to move across Manitoba through the day Friday and drop one to two inches of rain, he said.
Weekend temperatures should be normal at lows of 10 Celsius and highs of 25 Celsius.
Clouds over Alberta's foothills and the Calgary area may bring some showers on Sunday but no risk of frost.
The only location near but north of the Prairie grainbelt that has a remote chance of weekend frost is Thompson, Manitoba, on Sunday morning, Anderson said.
